prompt: For every segment, analyze pedestrian roadway behavior. Name any of these cases if present: (1) mid_block (2) red_hand (3) against_traffic (4) diagonal (5) between_cars. If only a legal marked-crosswalk crossing, write legal_crosswalk. If none, write none_observed.

cases.title: Against red hand / don't-walk
cases.summary: Pedestrians enter or continue through a marked crosswalk while the pedestrian signal shows a red hand or don't-walk.
cases.recommended_action: Extend pedestrian clearance (LPI + longer Walk) and add high-visibility countdown timers so walk phases match actual crossing demand.

videos.reasoning_content: Pedestrians are crossing the marked crosswalk while the pedestrian signal displays a red hand, indicating a violation of the traffic signal.
A pedestrian is crossing the street using the marked crosswalk. The traffic light is red, and the pedestrian is crossing legally.

cases.title: Crossing while cars move on green
cases.summary: Pedestrians cross an intersection while vehicles have a green signal and are moving through the conflict zone.
cases.recommended_action: Add Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI) and tighten turn-on-red / protected-only lefts to give walkers a head start before conflicting traffic moves.

videos.reasoning_content: At 0:25–0:30 (Clip 6), pedestrians are crossing the marked crosswalk while vehicles have a green light and are moving through the same conflict area, creating a near-miss situation.
Pedestrians are crossing the street at a marked crosswalk. The traffic light is green for vehicles, and pedestrians are using the crosswalk to cross the street.

A pedestrian is crossing the street using a marked crosswalk. The pedestrian is walking from left to right across the crosswalk. The traffic light is red for vehicles, indicating that pedestrians have the right of way. The pedestrian is not cutting diagonally across the intersection or stepping into moving traffic between cars. The pedestrian is not crossing mid-block outside a marked crosswalk.

cases.title: Diagonal cut off crosswalk lines
cases.summary: Pedestrians cut diagonally across an intersection, leaving the marked crosswalk lines and shortening the path through open pavement.
cases.recommended_action: Install scramble (Barnes Dance) phasing or corner curb extensions that make the legal two-leg path shorter and more obvious than a diagonal cut.

videos.reasoning_content: A pedestrian is crossing the street using a marked crosswalk. The pedestrian is walking from left to right across the crosswalk. The traffic light is red for vehicles, indicating that pedestrians have the right of way. The pedestrian is not cutting diagonally across the intersection or stepping into moving traffic between cars. The pedestrian is not crossing mid-block outside a marked crosswalk.
Pedestrians are using the marked crosswalk to cross the street. The traffic light is red, so vehicles are stopped. The pedestrians are crossing legally in the designated crosswalk area.

Pedestrians are crossing the street at a marked crosswalk. The traffic light is red, indicating that vehicles should stop and pedestrians have the right of way. The pedestrians are crossing legally and in an orderly manner. There are no instances of jaywalking, crossing against the signal, or cutting diagonally across the intersection.

cases.title: Mid-block outside marked crosswalk
cases.summary: Pedestrians cross mid-block outside a marked crosswalk, often where the nearest legal crossing feels too far.
cases.recommended_action: Add a midblock marked crosswalk with raised table or midblock fence/planting strip that channels desire lines to a controlled crossing.

videos.reasoning_content: Pedestrians are using a marked crosswalk to cross the street. The traffic light for pedestrians is showing a red hand, indicating that they should not enter the crosswalk. Vehicles are moving through the intersection while the pedestrians are waiting for the light to change. The pedestrians are not crossing the street at this time.
Pedestrians are crossing the street using the marked crosswalk. A silver car is driving through the intersection. The traffic light for pedestrians is showing a red hand.

cases.title: Into traffic between cars / off crosswalk
cases.summary: Pedestrians step into moving traffic between vehicles away from a marked crosswalk, weaving through gaps in the stream.
cases.recommended_action: Calm midblock speeds with turn calming / pinch points and continuous sidewalk fencing so gaps between cars are not a usable crossing path.

videos.reasoning_content: A pedestrian wearing a blue top and brown pants crosses the street using the marked crosswalk. The pedestrian is walking from left to right, moving across the intersection in a legal manner. The traffic light is red, indicating that vehicles should stop, and the pedestrian is crossing during this time. The pedestrian is not cutting diagonally across the intersection or stepping into moving traffic between cars.

Pedestrians are crossing the street at a marked crosswalk. The traffic light for pedestrians is showing a red hand, indicating that they should not be crossing. However, some pedestrians are still entering the crosswalk and beginning to cross. This is a violation of the traffic signal. The vehicles in the intersection have a green light and are moving through the intersection.

The scene is a busy city intersection with pedestrians crossing and vehicles moving through. A white SUV with blue markings and the text "ROAD CONTROL" is visible, indicating it is a police vehicle. Another white SUV follows behind it. A dark gray SUV is seen driving through the intersection from left to right. A large white truck is parked on the right side of the frame.

quality.rule: Always show up to 3 clips per case even if captions are weak matches.
